name: Nuvio for Apple TV
subtitle: Unsigned Nuvio builds for tvOS.
description: Official sideloading source for the NuvioTVOS repository. Releases are read directly from GitHub and remain unsigned until installed with your certificate.

apps.name: Nuvio
apps.subtitle: A native Nuvio client for Apple TV.
apps.localizedDescription: An unofficial, native tvOS client for the Stremio addon ecosystem, designed to match NuvioTV for Android TV while respecting Apple TV navigation and playback. The IPA is unsigned and must be signed with a tvOS-compatible certificate.

versions.localizedDescription:
**A proper app icon.**

The tvOS home screen was showing a dark square floating inside the rounded app bubble instead of
one unified icon. All three parallax layers held the same square logo file, background and all,
shrunk and centred in a frame it did not fit.

The icon is now three layers that each fill the frame — a brand-coloured field, a soft shadow of
the mark, and the mark itself — so it fills its bubble and moves with depth when you focus it.

**A playback stats overlay, ported from the Android app's latest releases.**

Turn it on in Settings → Advanced, then open **Stream information** during playback and press
**Stats**. It shows, live:

- **buffer** — how many seconds are ahead of the playhead, with a running average
- **network** — what the connection is actually delivering
- **bitrate** — what the file needs
- **cpu**, **memory**, **thermal** — the three reasons an Apple TV stutters

Network below bitrate is why something is buffering. A thermal reading that goes orange or red is
why an otherwise fine stream started stuttering twenty minutes in.

Off by default, and behind two steps rather than one — it is a diagnostic, not furniture.

**Holding Select on a poster now opens its options. It never did before.**

The menu itself has been in the app since 1.0.18 — add to or remove from your library, mark
watched, take something out of Continue Watching, manage your Trakt lists. Holding Select just
opened the title instead, so there was no way to reach any of it.

The same press now works everywhere it should:

- **Continue Watching** — remove a title from the row.
- **Library** — remove a title you saved.
- **Episodes** — mark one watched without playing it, or mark the season.
- **Profile chooser** — hold on a profile to manage it.

Marking something watched or removing it from Continue Watching was previously only possible
by playing it, or not possible at all.

## French, everywhere you actually watch

If your Apple TV is set to French, the whole viewing experience is now in French:
home, search, discover, your library, the Trakt and Simkl lists, the cloud
library, a title's page, cast, comments, the source list and the hand-off sheet,
the player and all its overlays, post-play, profiles and the sidebar.

**Settings is still English.** It is by far the largest part — 571 pieces of text
— and translating it properly is its own piece of work rather than the tail of
this one.

Nothing changes if your Apple TV is set to English.

## Under the hood

The app now refuses to build if a piece of text asks for a translation that does
not exist, exists in only one of the two languages, or is defined twice. That last
one is the quiet failure: two definitions, the second silently winning, so a
corrected translation can sit unused under a stale one.

## Your Trakt lists, from any poster

Long-press a poster and choose **Trakt lists…** to file it into one of your own
lists, or take it out. Your watchlist is not in there — that is what the library
row already does.

Which lists already hold the title fills in a moment after the dialog opens.
Trakt has no way to ask "which of my lists contain this", so it is one question
per list, and waiting on all of them before showing anything would be worse.

## Removing from Simkl asks first

Simkl stores a title's list state and its watched history as one record. Removing
it from your library there also clears every episode you had marked watched — so
it now asks before doing it.

Removing from Trakt does not ask, because on Trakt it only touches the watchlist.
Nothing else is lost, and a warning that fires when nothing is at stake is a
warning people learn to dismiss.

## Mark an episode watched

Long-press any episode on a series page. Until now there was no way to do this —
you either played the episode past the watched threshold, or marked the whole
series. Somebody who watched an episode elsewhere had no way to say so, and
Continue Watching kept offering it.

The dialog offers: play, start from the beginning, mark this episode, mark this
season, **mark this and everything before it**, and comments.

"Everything before it" crosses seasons — starting a show at season three and
marking everything before it watched means the earlier seasons, which is what you
meant.

Specials and episodes that have not aired are never marked.

## One show, one row

If you watch a series through two different addons, each one names it differently,
and Continue Watching used to show it twice — two rows for one show, each
suggesting a different next episode.

Now it is one row, following whichever addon you last watched it on.

## "Remember last profile" now tells the truth

The switch under Settings → Advanced showed **on** by default while every launch
behaved as though it were **off** — straight to "Who's watching?". Two parts of
the app disagreed about what the default was.

Nothing changes about how your Apple TV behaves. What changes is that the switch
now shows the state it is actually in, and turning it on works.

If you had already set it, your choice is kept.

## Syncing with Android TV

This setting was stored under a name Android TV does not use, so it was the one
preference that quietly failed to travel between the two apps. It now uses the
same name.

## Housekeeping

Four settings that appeared in the code but could never do anything on Apple TV
have been removed — decoder priority, subtitle renderer choice, Dolby Vision
profile 7 handling and cache sizing. libmpv either has no such choice to make or
has no such problem to solve.

## The rest of the franchise

A film that belongs to a series now shows the others on its page, under the
franchise's own name and above **More like this** — knowing there are two more
Dune films is a better answer to "what next" than a genre match.

In release order, and the film you are looking at is not in its own row.

Needs a TMDB API key, under Settings → Integrations.

## Removing from Continue Watching now sticks

If your watch progress comes from Trakt or Simkl, removing a row from Continue
Watching only removed it from this Apple TV. The next sync fetched the resume
point back from the service and the row returned, as though the removal had not
worked.

It now removes the resume point on the service too. Nothing else on your tracking
account is touched — the title's own resume points and nothing beyond them.

On the default local setting nothing changes; there was never anything remote to
bring the row back.

## Mark a whole series watched

Long-press any series poster and the **watched** row is there now, not just for
films. It marks every episode that has actually aired, and skips specials —
season zero is not part of the run you mean when you say you have watched a show.
Taking it back clears everything, specials included.

The row only appears once Nuvio knows the episode list, because a control that
reports success having marked nothing is worse than no control.

## Continue Watching stops waiting

Nuvio used to learn a series' episode list only when you opened its page. That
meant a show you started from the Home rail and never opened could not be offered
its next episode. The rail now fills that in for the shows at the front of it.

## Notes

Marking a series watched sends one request to Trakt or Simkl, not one per episode.

## Dialogue you can actually hear

A new **Dialogue level** control under Settings → Playback → Audio. It sets how
loud the centre channel is folded in when a 5.1 track is played through stereo —
the usual reason speech sits under the music. **Prevent downmix clipping** is
beside it, trading a little level for headroom.

Both are in Settings rather than in the player because libmpv builds its audio
chain from them when playback starts.

## Amplification that stays put

The player's amplification control can now be remembered between films. It is off
by default — amplification is usually the fix for one badly mastered release, and
carrying it forward is how everything ends up loud. Turning it on keeps whatever
level you are listening to.

## It tells you when it is out of date

Settings → About now says when a newer build has been published, and what changed.
It cannot install it — nothing sideloaded on tvOS can replace itself — but your
sideloading app will already be offering it if it follows the Nuvio source.

## Notes

Two audio settings from Android TV are not here and will not be: keeping the
original track alongside a downmix, and forced optical passthrough. The first is
an ExoPlayer arrangement libmpv has no equivalent of; the second needs an audio
passthrough API that tvOS does not have. Passthrough on Apple TV is decided by the
Apple TV's own audio settings.

## Badge rules

A source list can now say what you want it to say. Point the Apple TV at a badge
pack — a JSON file of named patterns with their own colours and logos — and every
matching source gets its badge. It uses the same file format as NuvioTV for
Android TV, so a pack written there works here unchanged.

Settings → Playback → Source list → **Badge rules**. Scan the code with a phone
on the same Wi-Fi; adding, swapping and removing packs all happen there. Three
packs can be held at once and one is applied.

## Plugin repositories, from a phone

The same idea for plugin repositories: the phone lists them and asks for changes,
and the **Apple TV asks you before anything happens**. Adding a repository
installs code that then runs on every stream search, and this page is visible to
your whole network — so the phone can only ask.

Settings → Addons → **Repositories**.

## Simkl now knows which episode you watched

Marking an episode watched sent Simkl the *show's* ids and nothing else — so it marked the whole series. Episode writes now name the episode.

## Anime

Simkl can be addressed two ways and they cannot be mixed: season coordinates, or an absolute number against a per-season entry. Sending both a franchise IMDb id and a per-season MyAnimeList id is not extra information — Simkl matches whichever it recognises first, and the episode lands on the wrong season of the wrong show.

The two shapes are now kept apart properly, with `use_tvdb_anime_seasons` telling Simkl which one it is looking at.

**Settings → Integrations → Simkl → Anime seasons** decides whether a franchise is one title or several. One IMDb id spans every season, while MyAnimeList and Kitsu give each its own entry — so grouping is right if you think of a show as one thing, and wrong if you track seasons separately. Your call now. Films and ordinary series are unaffected.

---

337 unit tests and 9 UI tests pass. The IPA is unsigned and must be signed with your own certificate.

## Continue Watching now offers the next episode

Until now the rail held only *half-watched* episodes. Finish one and the series left Home entirely — you had to go and find episode four yourself. That is the difference between "continue watching" and "things you gave up on partway".

A series whose last episode you finished is now offered its next one.

- **Unaired episodes are not offered.** An addon lists a whole season the day the first episode airs, so without this every currently-airing show would point at something that will not play. There is a setting if you want them anyway.
- **A caught-up series stays on the rail** when a new episode airs, rather than vanishing at the exact moment it becomes interesting again.
- **"Next up from furthest episode"** now means something: off, going back to rewatch episode two offers you three, instead of jumping past everything to the finale you saw out of order.

Hold Select on a suggestion to **stop being offered that show**. Watching it again brings it back.

The episode list is remembered when you open a series' page, so the rail can name the next episode instantly instead of waiting on an addon.

---

321 unit tests and 9 UI tests pass. The IPA is unsigned and must be signed with your own certificate.

## Edit the stream format from your phone

Nobody is going to type `{stream.size::>0["{stream.size::bytes} "||""]}` on a Siri Remote, so the Apple TV now serves the editor itself.

**Settings → Debrid → Stream format** shows a QR code. Scan it with a phone on the same Wi-Fi, edit the name and description there, and save — the preview on the television updates as you go.

The template language is Android's, reproduced rather than reinvented: a format written in the phone or Android TV app pastes in and produces the same rows. Conditions, comparisons, `and`/`or`, and transforms like `bytes`, `title` and `join(' | ')`. The shipped defaults are theirs byte for byte, so nothing changes unless you change it.

Applied only to results a debrid service will resolve. A direct HTTP source is already labelled the way its addon meant it.

The page is served on your local network only, from the Apple TV, and stops when you leave the screen.

---

299 unit tests and 9 UI tests pass. The IPA is unsigned and must be signed with your own certificate.

Six gaps the re-run parity audit turned up.

## Subtitles that arrive already broken

A subtitle file that some earlier tool read as Windows-1252 and wrote back out as UTF-8 is *itself* valid UTF-8 — so charset detection accepts it, correctly, and you get `Itâ€™s` where the author wrote `It's`. mpv's own auto-detection has the same blind spot for the same reason.

Nuvio now reverses the double encoding rather than matching known sequences, so Cyrillic, Greek and Japanese tracks come out right too — not just the Western European cases.

## Episode scores from the addon itself

Addons that publish `videos[].rating` now have it shown, in preference to the TMDB score. It is the only per-episode rating obtainable at all: the service Android uses sits behind a base URL that ships blank in its public source.

## Four settings

- **Rating visibility**, on Home and on a title's page — including *hide until watched*, since a 9.6 three episodes ahead tells you something happens there.
- **Hide the Continue Watching rail** entirely.
- **Rename an addon**, which survives the manifest being refetched.
- **Sort your library** by date added or title.

The rating-visibility controls are an apology as much as a feature: a previous audit withdrew them as "not a parity item" while reading an older tree than the release it named.

---

266 unit tests and 9 UI tests pass. The IPA is unsigned and must be signed with your own certificate.

## Hold Select on any poster

`clearProgress` has existed in the library store since the library store did, and nothing in the app has ever called it — a resume point could be created from anywhere and removed from nowhere. The only way to clear a Continue Watching row was to finish the thing.

Holding Select on any poster — Home, Discover, Search, Library, a collection folder, the Continue Watching rail — now opens a dialog with:

- **Add to / Remove from Library**
- **Mark as watched / unwatched** (films)
- **Remove from Continue Watching**
- **Go to details**

Library and watched writes go through the same path the detail screen uses, so with Trakt or Simkl connected they land on the account you read from.

Two things deliberately not offered yet: marking a whole *series* watched, which needs an episode walk that does not exist here, and Trakt list management.

---

236 unit tests and 9 UI tests pass. The IPA is unsigned and must be signed with your own certificate.

## Scrubbing no longer covers what you are scrubbing through

With the controls hidden, pressing left or right used to bring the whole transport bar up and *then* seek — the bar landing over the bottom of the frame you were hunting through. It now seeks in place behind a compact readout: the target time, how far the jump has travelled, and where that sits in the film. Up or down still brings the transport back, and holding a direction still accelerates.

The readout is a label, never a control. It stays out of the focus graph, so the next press reaches the player rather than landing on it.

## Parity audit re-run against Android TV 0.8.9-beta

The previous audit named 0.8.7-beta but measured an older commit, so several "missing upstream" findings were made against the wrong tree. Corrected, along with three claims that came out of it — including the IMDb rating-visibility controls, which had been withdrawn as "not a parity item" when they had in fact shipped in the tag named.

**Torrents now require a debrid service, stated plainly.** This was never a choice to make: upstream runs TorrServer as a native binary in a subprocess, which tvOS does not permit at all.

Full comparison in [`docs/PARITY-AUDIT.md`](https://github.com/vatax3/NuvioTVOS/blob/main/docs/PARITY-AUDIT.md).

---

226 unit tests and 9 UI tests pass. The IPA is unsigned and must be signed with your own certificate.

## Pausing kept the Apple TV awake

The wake lock was held for the whole presentation regardless of playback state, so a film left on Pause overnight held the idle timer off all night.

The obvious fix is wrong, and the code already said why: releasing the lock whenever playback is not running does not survive contact with a stream, because **every buffer stall and every track change passes through a non-playing state**. Re-arming the idle timer on each of those is what used to put the device to sleep mid-film.

So the two are told apart by how long the pause lasts rather than by the fact of it. A stall is seconds; somebody walking away is not.

**After two minutes paused, the idle timer is re-armed** and the television sleeps on its own schedule. The system's Sleep After starts counting from there, so even its shortest setting still gives you seventeen minutes. The hold itself is kept, so resuming re-asserts immediately.

Two details that would have broken it quietly: a paused player emits no further events, so the pause arms its own timer — nothing else would re-evaluate the rule; and the minute heartbeat that re-asserts the lock now goes through the same rule instead of forcing the flag back on, or it would have undone the release two minutes later.

## Episode scores

Episode air dates were already shown; scores were not. Reading the Android source shows why they could not simply be added: the per-episode **IMDb** figure comes from two services whose base URLs are build secrets resolving to `placeholder.nuvio.tv` in the public source — a private contract, like the discovery endpoint.

TMDB's own score is not. It arrives in the same season response the titles, overviews, stills and air dates already come from; the field was being decoded away one line from where it was needed. So the row shows a score, and it is TMDB's rather than IMDb's. A zero from TMDB means nobody has scored the episode, so it is dropped rather than shown as zero.

## Verification

217 unit tests, 8 UI tests, 0 failures. The wake-lock rule is a pure function with the buffer-stall case pinned as its own test.

The sleep behaviour needs a real Apple TV and a real wait to confirm — reported as fixed, not observed.

Unsigned IPA — sideload with your usual signer.

## Add to Library was a broken button

Reads were routed to Trakt and Simkl; writes were not. The Library screen shows the Trakt list and nothing else when the library source is Trakt, while the detail screen's Add button wrote to the local store — so a viewer on Trakt pressed Add and watched the title disappear. Saved on the device, read from a list it had never been sent to.

It now reaches the account. The rule is **local always, remote in addition**: the local copy survives an expired token and a flight-mode launch, and it is the only record left if the remote request fails. The detail screen says when a save reached the device but not the account, because silence is how the original bug hid.

Trakt answers 201 for a title it did not recognise and reports the miss in `not_found`, so a status code alone can no longer pass a write that changed nothing off as success.

The watched path is deliberately untouched — the player already scrobbles a stop at 100%, which is what marks a title watched on both accounts.

## Sign in to TorBox with a code

A debrid API key is forty characters and the only way in was the on-screen keyboard. TorBox hands back a short code, you approve it on a phone, and the key arrives on its own.

TorBox only: Premiumize's device flow needs a client id that really is absent from upstream's public source, and Real-Debrid has no device flow at all. The row is only drawn for a provider that can honour it.

## The audit withdrew two items that were not parity

Both endpoints above were ported by reading the Android source rather than guessing, and that reading corrected the audit twice: upstream has **no** `sync/collection` call, and Simkl has no list-removal call — removing from a list is removing from history.

Two of the three remaining P2 entries did not survive the same check:

- **IMDb rating-visibility settings do not exist upstream.** Every preference key containing "rating" or "visib" in 0.8.7-beta is a JSON field name in an API DTO, not a setting. Building the controls would have been inventing a feature and filing it as parity.
- **Top Shelf already carries remote progress.** Trakt and Simkl resume points are adopted into the same store that publishes the shelf. Nothing to build.

They are struck through rather than deleted. An audit that invents work is a worse failure than one that misses some.

Parity now stands at 18 of 28 areas at the expected level, 8 partial, 2 missing — one of those by decision.

## Verification

205 unit tests, 8 UI tests, 0 failures. 17 new contract tests assert the method, path, auth headers and body of every write against a stubbed session — these endpoints mutate a real library, so they must never reach one during development.

Not verified against live Trakt, Simkl or TorBox accounts. That remains an acceptance test, not a claim.

Unsigned IPA — sideload with your usual signer.

Four fixes in the mpv player. Three were salvaged from a parked branch where they had been mixed in with remux work that is not ready; they had nothing to do with it.

## Subtitles now clear the edge of the television

`sub-pos` was computed as `100 - offset/10`, and the stored offset defaults to zero — so the default was **100**, which puts the line against the physical bottom of the frame. That strip is exactly what a television overscans away. Every viewer had this on muxed subtitle tracks.

It now starts at 90, inside the title-safe area, with mpv's margins enabled so text is laid out inside the frame rather than against it. A positive offset still moves the line upward.

## The bundled CJK font reaches mpv

Registering the Noto CJK face with CoreText was never enough: libass loads fonts through FreeType and does not consult the process registration. The face was visible to Swift and still rendered as tofu. It now gets the directory as a font source too.

## Changing audio or subtitle track no longer cuts the sound

mpv demuxes only the streams that are selected, so picking a new track makes it seek back to the playhead to collect that stream's packets. `demuxer-max-back-bytes` defaults to zero, so that seek went to the network — one to two seconds of silence, every time, on a debrid or HTTP source.

A 32 MiB backward buffer with a seekable cache serves the same seek from memory, and the switch happens under the picture.

## Smaller

- The viewer's default picture shape is applied before `loadfile`, so the first frame already has it instead of snapping out of Fit a beat later.
- `.focusEffectDisabled()` on the in-player panel rows, source rows and rail cards — the same tvOS 26 focus plate fixed on the skip and post-play cards in 1.0.9, on the surfaces that pass was not looking at.

## Verification

182 unit tests, 8 UI tests, 0 failures. Built from a clean tree at the release commit.

The track switch and the subtitle position need a real stream and a real television to confirm — reported as fixed in principle, not as observed.

Unsigned IPA — sideload with your usual signer.

Fixes a regression that locked people out of their own Nuvio account.

## What was wrong

The app shipped with an empty Supabase publishable key, on the reasoning that the official Android app reads it from `local.properties` at build time and so could not be redistributed. The reasoning was sound; the premise was wrong — the key is in Nuvio's public API docs, and this app's own earlier tvOS build carried it citing them. A `sb_publishable_` key is meant to live in the client: row-level security protects the rows, not the obscurity of the key.

The cost was not a missing convenience. An empty key refuses **both** the QR flow and email/password at once, so the failure had no way out from inside the app.

It surfaced through an asymmetry worth recording: the session lives in the keychain, the server configuration lives in a file in the app container. Deleting an app on Apple platforms clears the container and leaves the keychain — so a reinstall was still signed in but no longer configured. It kept working on the stored token until you signed out, which removed the only thing holding it together.

## What changed

- Nuvio's backend URL **and** key ship again. Nothing to paste to use a Nuvio account.
- A configuration that lost its key is repaired, at launch and on save. Emptying the fields now lands back on Nuvio's own backend.
- A self-hosted instance with no key is left exactly as it is — Nuvio's key would not authenticate against someone else's project, and writing it there would trade a legible "not configured" for a baffling 401.
- The account screen's copy no longer tells you to paste something that is already there.
- A test now asserts the shipped default is usable, which is what nothing did before. It was verified to fail: blanking the key turns four of its eight tests red.

## Verification

206 unit tests, 8 UI tests, 0 failures. Built from a clean tree at the release commit.

Unsigned IPA — sideload with your usual signer.
